limitations: This is a deterministic tracked-source signal census, not a complete call graph.
Comments and path names are leads and do not establish hardware contracts.
Generated build output, binaries, archives, logs, and private documents are not scanned.
PC-98/NEC98 source evidence does not establish PC-88VA behavior.

routing_policy.membership_count_semantics: Milestone membership counts overlap and are not task counts, effort estimates, or an exclusive partition of the census.

rules.description: Assembly text contains an interrupt instruction or interrupt return lead.
rules.notes: The scanner does not infer vector numbers or calling conventions from this token.

rules.description: Assembly text contains an input/output instruction lead.
rules.notes: Instruction syntax is recorded as a lead; port numbers and device semantics require review.

rules.description: Tracked source or build text names boot, loader, IPL, or boot-sector layout.
rules.notes: Boot naming is NEC98/source evidence only; it is not a VA IPL claim.

rules.description: Source text names an include relationship.
rules.notes: The scanner records the textual relationship without resolving compiler search paths.

rules.description: Build/configuration text selects a platform, compiler, model, or language variant.
rules.notes: A conditional or build variable is a selection lead, not a complete build graph.

rules.description: Comment text names a platform or hardware lead for human review.
rules.notes: Comments are leads only and are never sufficient hardware evidence.

rules.description: Tracked text names keyboard, enhanced input, terminal, or console input.
rules.notes: Input naming is a port-surface lead and not a Japanese-runtime validation.

rules.description: Tracked text names console, character, printer, screen, or display output.
rules.notes: Output path names are not evidence of a VA firmware or video register contract.

rules.description: Tracked text names devices, drivers, or initialization paths.
rules.notes: Initialization order and device names require an explicit later contract.

rules.description: Tracked text names disk, FAT, BPB, sector, media, geometry, or block I/O behavior.
rules.notes: The hit identifies a source surface; geometry and firmware semantics remain unresolved.

rules.description: Tracked text names DMA, FDC, floppy, or controller operations.
rules.notes: NEC98 controller references cannot be promoted to a VA contract without VA evidence.

rules.description: Tracked text names command execution, shell, SYS, spawn, or runtime transfer.
rules.notes: A command/runtime hit does not claim that a NEC98 binary runs on VA.

rules.description: Tracked text names BIOS, firmware, port I/O, or low-level firmware calls.
rules.notes: PC-98 BIOS references are not PC-88VA evidence.

rules.description: Tracked text names interrupts, IRQ, PIC, vectors, or interrupt handlers.
rules.notes: Interrupt references are source observations and do not define VA vector ownership.

rules.candidate_boundary: pc88va load, segment, and startup contract
rules.description: Tracked text names memory, segments, stack, startup, or memory-resident services.
rules.notes: Names identify startup-sensitive code but do not resolve VA addresses or register state.

rules.description: Tracked text names Country, NLS, DBCS, Japanese, or codepage behavior.
rules.notes: NLS data and DBCS logic are separate from unresolved VA hardware services.

rules.description: Tracked path names the IBM PC platform directory.
rules.notes: Path evidence identifies a platform variant; it does not establish hardware equivalence.

rules.description: Tracked path names the NEC98 platform directory.
rules.notes: Path evidence identifies a platform variant; it does not establish VA hardware behavior.

rules.description: Tracked text names timer, clock, tick, or time initialization.
rules.notes: Timer names do not establish interrupt frequency or BIOS time semantics.
